questions.q: Why did United States Treasury yields drift near the 5% threshold?
o: Coordinated monetary tightening by the Federal Reserve and the Bank of Japan intersected with commodity shocks.
The Federal Reserve lowered benchmark interest rates to combat slowing growth across commercial sectors.
Commercial banks increased their sovereign debt holdings following unexpected fiscal surpluses.
Foreign central banks aggressively dumped dollar-denominated assets to support domestic emerging market currencies.
questions.e: Sovereignty debt yields approached 5% as coordinated tightening by the Federal Reserve and the Bank of Japan intersected with commodity shocks. Energy-driven inflation expectations forced duration repricing across the curve. The other options contradict the stated facts regarding policy direction and market drivers.

Traders ignored the inflation print because fiscal policy dictates borrowing costs entirely.
Traders demanded immediate quantitative easing from the central bank.
questions.e: U.K. headline inflation prints ticked higher on the eve of the Monetary Policy Committee rate decision, which complicated policy optionality and led traders to adjust rate cut probabilities. The other choices involve actions not supported by the text.
